6. Risk category and supporting evidence

Cardiac risk assessment: not available. Predicting heart risk needs a model trained and checked on follow-up outcome data, and this project has none. An ECG alone cannot predict a person's overall heart risk, so no risk level or percentage is shown.

7. Confidence and limitations

  • Each measurement above carries the error we measured for its method; the traffic light is the per-photo check.
  • The findings model was trained on public hospital ECGs and tested on our drawn pages and phone photos; findings that did not pass the pre-set tests are not shown.
  • A 'not found' result misses some patterns: in our phone-photo tests the checks found about 79 in 100 infarction patterns, 72 in 100 ST/T patterns and 86 in 100 conduction patterns, and wrongly flagged 16 to 24 in 100 photos without the pattern.
  • Model confidence is not heart risk.
  • One phone, one screen and drawn pages were tested; printed paper and other phones are not yet shown to work.

8. Recommended next steps

Please show this ECG and this result to a doctor for medical evaluation. Get medical help straight away for chest pain, fainting, breathlessness or a racing heartbeat.

This is an AI-assisted research assessment, not a medical diagnosis. It is not a medical device and does not replace a doctor or a cardiologist. A normal-looking ECG does not exclude heart disease, and an ECG alone cannot predict a person's overall heart risk.
